newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Surgical says Ethicon suit dismissed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Surgical says Ethicon suit dismissed.

text.p: United States Surgical Corp said on Tuesday a U.S. District Court judge entered an order dismissing in its entirety Johnson & Johnson unit Ethicon Inc's trocar patent infringement claim against U.S. Surgical.
The company said this cleared the way for it to proceed with its patent infringement claims against Ethicon over trocar, a surgical device.
Ethicon was not immediately available for comment.

U.S. Surgical said Ethicon was allegedly infringing on three of its trocar patents. The Ethicon products at issue include all safety-shielded trocars sold by Ethicon since their introduction in 1990, it said.
U.S. Surgical said it estimated these sales exceeded $1 billion.

Johnson & Johnson spokesman Jeff Leeblaw later said: "We're disappointed with the decision, we think it's erroneous and we plan to appeal." Johnson & Johnson sued U.S. Surgical over trocar patent infringement in 1989 and U.S. Surgical filed a countersuit, the company said.
Trocars are cylindrical tubes through which doctors insert scopes and instruments during minimally-invasive surgery.
U.S. Surgical said there were two inventors of a particular trocar design. One sold the rights to U.S. Surgical and the other inventor sold the rights to Johnson & Johnson, it said.
